title: Observability ops cheatsheet: VPC & on-prem installs + TF module notes
body:
Purpose:
This is an operational cheatsheet and install/upgrade checklist for running observability in private deployments (VPC or on-prem). It combines quick TF module notes, deployment patterns for Prometheus/Grafana and OTEL collectors, log shipping options, and a conservative upgrade plan we can run with minimal customer impact.

Scope:
- Target envs: customer VPCs (AWS/GCP), private datacenters (k8s or VM-based clusters).
- Components: Prometheus (scrape + recording rules + federation), Grafana (provisioning + dashboards), OTEL collectors (metrics/logs/traces via OTLP), log shippers (Fluent Bit / Filebeat / OTEL logs), remote_write/long term store (Thanos / Cortex / S3).
- Not in scope: hosted API infra, telemetry from Redwood public services.

Quick top-level layout (typical reference):
- Network: inside VPC only, collector endpoints bound to internal ILB, mTLS or IP allowlist for ingestion.
- In-cluster: OTEL collector(s) run as DaemonSet for logs/metrics, one or more observable-aggregator deployments for heavy CPU work (ingest batching, exporters).
- Metrics: Prometheus (k8s: kube-prometheus-stack) scrapes pod/service endpoints via ServiceMonitors. Prometheus remote_write -> Cortex/Thanos for long term.
- Dashboards: Grafana backed by Prometheus/Cortex datasources. Dashboard provisioning via configmaps or file provisioning (gitops).

Terraform module notes (practical):
- Module layout we use: 
  - modules/observability/networking -> creates internal LB, DNS records, SGs (variables: cluster_id, allowed_cidrs, tls_cert_arn)
  - modules/observability/prometheus -> helm_release resource for kube-prometheus-stack (vars: prometheus_retention, scrape_interval, prometheus_replicas)
  - modules/observability/grafana -> grafana provisioning + admin user rotation (vars: dashboards_git_repo, smtp_cfg)
  - modules/observability/otel -> helm_release for otel-collector with exporter config templated via templatefile() (vars: collector_mode {daemonset|deployment}, otlp_endpoint, exporter_backends)
  - modules/observability/log-shipper -> optional, choices: fluent-bit/filebeat/otel-logs (vars: shipper_type, s3_bucket, siem_endpoint)
- Remote state: always use backend with customer-controlled storage (S3/GCS) and lock (DynamoDB). Avoid shared global state across customers.
- Versioning: pin module versions and chart versions. Example: chart_version = "45.1.0". Add tfvars with immutable tag for production.
- Outputs: expose internal endpoints (prometheus_endpoint, grafana_endpoint, otel_ingest_url) and IAM role ARNs for exporters. Keep outputs minimal and tag secrets as sensitive in TF state.
- Workspaces: use per-environment workspace (dev/staging/prod) and CI pipeline that runs terraform plan and stores plan artifacts in build logs.

Sample TF usage (pseudocode):
- terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${var.tf_state_bucket}" \n  -var="cluster_name=${var.cluster_name}"
- module "prometheus" {
    source = "../../modules/observability/prometheus"
    prometheus_retention = "15d"
    chart_version = "45.1.0"
  }

Prometheus specific notes:
- Scrape topology: use serviceMonitor relabeling to drop high-cardinality labels before ingest. Example relabel_configs to drop pod_ip and instance for certain endpoints (add in values.yaml).
- Recording rules: precompute heavy aggregations (p90, p99, error rates) to reduce query load. Keep recordings in a separate config map and apply atomically.
- Retention: use short local retention (15d) + remote_write to Cortex/Thanos for >30d. Beware memory spikes on compactions.
- High-availability: run 2 replicas of Prometheus with active-passive or use Thanos sidecar for HA. Docs: https://prometheus.io/docs
- Security: Prometheus endpoint behind internal ALB, basic auth or mTLS for federation endpoints.

Grafana provisioning and ops:
- Provisioning: store dashboards and datasources in git and use provisioning.yaml mounted via configmap. Automation: CI job that validates JSON dashboards with grafonnet or grafana-toolkit.
- Admin creds: avoid embedding admin passwords; use vault/kms to inject during bootstrap. Rotate admin password on major upgrades.
- Alerts: route alerts to customer-defined on-call systems. Keep escalation policy in customer repo.

OTEL collector and logging:
- Deployment mode: prefer DaemonSet for logs (local tailing), Deployment for centralized metric/trace ingestors with autoscale.
- Pipelines: keep basic pipelines for metrics/traces/logs. Use batching and compression exporters to reduce egress.
- Exporters: configure exporters to target internal Cortex/Thanos/Jaeger endpoints. For logs, prefer sending to S3 (compressed + encrypted) or to customer SIEM if real-time required.
- Resource sizing: collectors can be CPU heavy with tailing. Start with request: 200m/256Mi and scale to 1/1Gi for heavy workloads.

Log shipping patterns (tradeoffs):
- Filebeat: lightweight, good for structured logs; easier multiline handling.
- Fluent Bit: low memory, good Kubernetes integration; use when you need minimal footprint.
- OTEL logs: consolidates metrics/traces/logs, easier instrumentation end-to-end but collectors are heavier.
- Storage: sending logs to S3 (parquet/json gz) + Athena/Presto is cheap. If customer needs searchable SIEM, route to Splunk/Datadog/ELK and plan for retention costs.

Upgrade strategy (conservative, low-risk):
1) Pre-flight: run terraform plan, validate chart versions in staging, run smoke dashboards validation (CI).
2) Collector canary: deploy new collector image to 5% of nodes (label-based). Verify CPU/RAM/ingest rates and no data loss for 1–2 hours.
3) Prometheus config changes: apply recording rules in staging, then roll to prod with 1 pod at a time (avoid joint head-of-line issues). If using Thanos, update sidecars carefully.
4) Grafana: provision dashboards first to staging. For major upgrades, create a backup of grafana DB (sqlite/pg). Apply upgrade during low-traffic window.
5) Terraform change ordering: separate infra changes (LB, DNS, SG) from app upgrades. Use two-step plan/app pattern: plan -> apply infra -> wait -> apply app.
6) Rollback: keep previous terraform state snapshots and helm chart versions. If rollbacks are needed for helm charts, use helm rollback with preserved PVCs.
7) Post-upgrade verification: query sample dashboards, compare recording rule outputs, check alert delivery (test alerts), run log tail to ensure no gaps.

Checklist for release (copyable):
- [ ] terraform plan validated and reviewed (ENG-1873)
- [ ] backup grafana DB snapshot created
- [ ] prometheus ruleset linted and staged
- [ ] canary collectors deployed and monitored for 2h
- [ ] remote_write connectivity tested (auth + TLS)
- [ ] log shipping end-to-end validated to S3/SIEM
- [ ] runbook updated with rollback steps

Operational gotchas & notes to self:
- Prometheus memory grows nonlinearly with number of series; keep cardinality caps and use relabeling aggressively.
- OTEL collector configs get messy: prefer templating collector config via Helm values and keep a minimal baseline per-customer.
- When shipping logs to S3, prefer batching and gzip to reduce PUT overhead. Consider lifecycle rules to transition to infrequent tiers.
- Watch for kube DNS limits when many exporters talk to internal endpoints; use cluster-local DNS caching where possible.
- Avoid exposing Grafana to the public internet; if necessary, use strict IP allowlists + OIDC + MFA.

Open questions / decisions:
- Decision: Do we recommend OTEL logs as default for on-prem vs Fluent Bit? (action: Priya to prototype both on customer staging) -> ENG-1921
- Should we maintain a single canonical tf module for all customers or fork per-cloud-provider? (action: Diego to write pros/cons doc)
- Long term store: Cortex vs Thanos for scale/cost tradeoff — need a cost model for 100k series/day (Oliver)

Action items (owners):
- Maya: template example tfvars for observability baseline (due 2025-10-10)
- Priya: run OTEL vs FluentBit POC in lab cluster (due 2025-10-03)
- Diego: draft module versioning policy + workspace layout doc (ENG-1908)

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- helm upgrade/install prometheus:
  helm upgrade --install prometheus prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack -n monitoring -f values-prometheus.yaml --version 45.1.0
- grafana provisioning check:
  kubectl -n monitoring exec deploy/grafana -- grafana-cli admin --help || echo \"check provisioning\"
- terraform plan for observability:
  terraform init -backend-config="bucket=${var.tf_state_bucket}" && terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars
- otel collector logs tail (k8s):
  kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/otel-collector -f

If anything here blocks you in a customer rollout, ping #eng-private-deploy on Slack and reference the ticket above. This doc is intended as a living cheatsheet — keep it terse and add steps you actually ran during live upgrades.

Notes to self: keep a small set of example dashboards (k8s overview, latency p95/p99, error-rate service map) in grafana repo. Avoid dumping huge generic dashboards into customer accounts; tailor to their SLOs.

Last revision notes: added more TF module guidance (Sep 15 2025) and canary collector step (Oct 02 2025).
